finding.statement: Brampton Gurdon of Assington's letter to John Winthrop, 20 October 1627, asks Winthrop — then an attorney at the Court of Wards and Liveries — to further a clergyman's suit to the Master of the Wards over a church presentation held by 'mrs. Gurny who is gardyon to her sonn who wantethe a few monthes of being of ful age,' whom 'yong mr. gurney' attends, with commendations to Emmanuel Downing. It is the only Gurney-variant document in the whole Winthrop Family Papers.

finding.statement: The clergyman 'mr. Warford' whom Mrs. Gurney presented in 1627 is unidentified: no Warford of any spelling appears in Venn's Alumni Cantabrigienses (to 1751), and none in Foster's Oxford register beyond too-early Bristol men. The Norwich diocesan institution registers (the Clergy of the Church of England Database) are the remaining route, and his institution would name the Gurney-held advowson.

finding.shortLabel: Blomefield: the Gurney-held West Barsham living, its 1603-1743 institution gap, and the excluded Norfolk livings

sources.alignmentNote: Gurney patron of West Barsham 1603; no West Barsham institution printed 1603-1743; Harpley and Great Ellingham excluded as the 1627 living.
sources.locator: West Barsham vicars list and Gurney patronage 1603 (vol. vii, pp. 42-47); Harpley rectors (vol. viii, pp. 452-459); Great Ellingham vicars (Hundred of Shropham, 1628 Scot institution)

finding.statement: Blomefield's parish histories locate the 1627 presentation on the West Barsham side. At West Barsham (vol. vii, pp. 42-47) the Gurneys held the vicarage advowson - 'In 1603, Leonard Metcalf occurs vicar, and certified 420 communicants; patron then, Henry Gurney' (Henry G15) - and the printed vicars list records no institution between 1603 and 1743, so a c.1627-28 presentation of Warford there is invisible in Blomefield; a competing Fermor advowson interest is also on record (William Fermor lord 'with the advowson' in 1627). The two other Gurney-associated Norfolk livings are excluded for 1627: Harpley (vol. viii, pp. 452-459) was held 1620-1648 by Edmund Gurnay B.D. under Sir William Yelverton, its advowson long out of the family, and Great Ellingham's one institution in the window (7 Nov 1628) was an Earl of Sussex presentation. West Barsham - where the heir Edward was in ward - is therefore the leading candidate for the presentation, with the Crown the likely patron of record during the minority whoever held the advowson in fee.
